```python
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# TSDA-chain demo.
# three floating boxes linked together (and to the ground) by TSDA
# springs without gravity.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parameters
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
rest_length   = 1.5
spring_coef   = 50.0
damping_coef  = 1.0
step_size     = 1e-3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create the physical system
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sys = chrono.ChSystemNSC()
sys.Set_G_acc(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0))       # no gravity

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ground (fixed reference body)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
ground = chrono.ChBody()
ground.SetBodyFixed(True)
ground.SetCollide(False)
sys.Add(ground)

# small sphere on the ground to visualise the world origin
sph = chrono.ChSphereShape()
sph.GetSphereGeometry().rad = 0.1
ground.AddAsset(sph)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper routine for creating a coloured box body
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
def make_box(name, position, color_rgb):
    body = chrono.ChBody()
    body.SetPos(position)
    body.SetMass(1.0)
    body.SetInertiaXX(chrono.ChVectorD(1, 1, 1))
    body.SetCollide(False)

    box = chrono.ChBoxShape()
    box.GetBoxGeometry().Size = chrono.ChVectorD(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
    box.SetColor(chrono.ChColor(*color_rgb))
    body.AddAsset(box)

    sys.Add(body)
    return body

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Floating bodies
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
body_1 = make_box("body_1", chrono.ChVectorD(-1.0, -3.0, 0.0), (0.6, 0.0, 0.0))
body_2 = make_box("body_2", chrono.ChVectorD( 0.0, -3.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.6, 0.0))
body_3 = make_box("body_3", chrono.ChVectorD( 1.0, -3.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0, 0.6))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Springs (TSDA links)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
def make_tsda(name, bodyA, bodyB, posA, posB):
    tsda = chrono.ChLinkTSDA()
    tsda.Initialize(bodyA, bodyB, True, posA, posB)
    tsda.SetRestLength(rest_length)
    tsda.SetSpringCoefficient(spring_coef)
    tsda.SetDampingCoefficient(damping_coef)

    # nice coil visualisation
    tsda_visual = chrono.ChSpringShape()
    tsda_visual.SetRadius(0.05)
    tsda.AddAsset(tsda_visual)

    sys.AddLink(tsda)
    return tsda

# ground ↔ body_1
spring_1 = make_tsda("spring_1", body_1, ground,
                     chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0),   # body_1 local
                     chrono.ChVectorD(-1, 0, 0))  # ground local

# body_1 ↔ body_2
spring_2 = make_tsda("spring_2", body_1, body_2,
                     chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0),
                     chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0))

# body_2 ↔ body_3
spring_3 = make_tsda("spring_3", body_2, body_3,
                     chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0),
                     chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bind and update all assets so that the Irrlicht vis. system can see them
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
chrono.AssetBindAll(sys)
chrono.AssetUpdateAll(sys)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Irrlicht visualisation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(sys)
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)
vis.SetWindowTitle("TSDA chain demo")
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile("logo_pychrono_alpha.png"))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 6))
vis.AddTypicalLights()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simulation loop
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()

    sys.DoStepDynamics(step_size)
```

    “”"
    Generate a PyChrono script that demonstrates a single mass-spring-damper system using `ChLinkTSDA` to connect a mass to the ground. Ensure the simulation includes Irrlicht visualization with appropriate lighting and camera settings, and provide visual shapes for the mass and spring in the scene. # =============================================================================
```python
# Basic PyChrono example:
# A single mass connected to ground through a linear spring–damper (ChLinkTSDA)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# – includes Irrlicht 3-D visualization (sky, lights, camera)
# – shows a box for the moving mass and a coil-like graphic for the TSDA link
# =============================================================================
#
# Tested with ProjectChrono 7.*  /  Python ≥ 3.8
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.irrlicht as irr

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create the physical system
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sys = chrono.ChSystemSMC()          # (or ChSystemNSC – either works here)
sys.Set_G_acc(chrono.ChVectorD(0, -9.81, 0))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create (fixed) ground
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
ground = chrono.ChBody()
ground.SetBodyFixed(True)
sys.Add(ground)

# Optional: a thin box to see the ground in the 3-D window
ground_visual = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(3.0, 0.1, 3.0,          # size (x,y,z)
                                     1000,                   # density  (irrelevant for fixed)
                                     True, True)             # collide?, visual?
ground_visual.SetBodyFixed(True)
ground_visual.SetPos(chrono.ChVectorD(0, -0.05, 0))
sys.Add(ground_visual)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Create the moving mass (a small cube)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
mass          = 1.0                          # kg
size          = 0.2                          # box edge length (m)
initial_pos   = chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0.5, 0)  # starting location

cube = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(size, size, size,
                            mass,
                            True,  True)      # collide?, visualize?
cube.SetPos(initial_pos)

# The default inertias from ChBodyEasy* are fine for this demo, but we can set
# them explicitly if desired:
Ixx = Iyy = Izz = (1/6) * mass * size**2
cube.SetInertiaXX(chrono.ChVectorD(Ixx, Iyy, Izz))

sys.Add(cube)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Add the spring–damper (TSDA) between ground and cube
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
k   = 100.0   # [N/m] spring stiffness
c   =   5.0   # [N·s/m] damping coefficient
rest_length = 0.40  # [m] spring free length

# End-points of the link (expressed in global coordinates)
pos_ground = chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0.00, 0)                 # on ground
pos_cube   = chrono.ChVectorD(0, +size/2, 0)              # top face of cube

tsda = chrono.ChLinkTSDA()
tsda.Initialize(ground, cube, False, pos_ground, pos_cube)
tsda.SetSpringCoefficient(k)
tsda.SetDampingCoefficient(c)
tsda.SetRestLength(rest_length)

# Ask Chrono to generate a simple coil-like visualization for the TSDA
# (radius, number_of_turns, color):
tsda.AddVisualShapeSpring(0.02, 20, chrono.ChColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.9))

sys.Add(tsda)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Irrlicht application (visualization)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
app = irr.ChIrrApp(sys,
                   "Single mass–spring–damper (ChLinkTSDA) demo",
                   irr.dimension2du(1024, 768))

app.AddTypicalLogo()
app.AddTypicalSky()

# Two point lights
app.AddTypicalLights(chrono.ChVectorD(+2, 4, -2),
                     chrono.ChVectorD(-2, 4, +2), 9, 1)

# Camera: (position, target)
app.AddCamera(chrono.ChVectorD(1.5, 1.0, 1.5),
              chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0.25, 0))

# Tell Irrlicht to use the visual assets we attached
app.AssetBindAll()
app.AssetUpdateAll()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Simulation main loop
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
time_step = 1e-3
app.SetTimestep(time_step)

while app.GetDevice().run():
    app.BeginScene()
    app.DrawAll()
    app.DoStep()          # advances dynamics by 'time_step'
    app.EndScene()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# End of file
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
```

How it works
• A `ChBodyEasyBox` is used for the 1 kg mass; its top face is the upper attachment point for the TSDA.  
• A `ChLinkTSDA` connects that point to a point on the fixed ground.  Default linear behaviour is specified through `SetSpringCoefficient()`, `SetDampingCoefficient()`, and `SetRestLength()`.  
• `AddVisualShapeSpring()` (added in Chrono 6.0+) generates a helix between the two attachment nodes so you can see the spring stretching/contracting during the run.  
• The Irrlicht helper (`ChIrrApp`) provides a ready-to-use window with lights, sky, and camera, while `DoStep()` keeps physics and graphics synchronized.

```python
#  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  ChLinkTSDA example with a user-defined force functor
#
#  This script shows two identical bodies that are each attached to the ground
#  by a translational spring–damper (TSDA).  The first spring uses the built-in
#  linear‐elastic / linear-damping law, whereas the second one relies on a user
#  force functor (MySpringForce).  Two small spheres are placed on the ground
#  to mark the attachment points of the springs.
#  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simulation parameters
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
rest_length   = 1.5          # unloaded length of both springs
spring_coef   = 50.0         # stiffness  [N/m]
damping_coef  = 1.0          # damping    [N·s/m]
time_step     = 1.0e-3       # integrator step size

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create the physical system
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
sys = chrono.ChSystemNSC()

# (no gravity so the motion is produced only by the springs)
try:                                     # depending on Chrono version
    sys.SetGravitationalAcceleration(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0))
except AttributeError:
    sys.Set_G_acc(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ground body (immobile reference)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ground = chrono.ChBody()
ground.SetBodyFixed(True)
ground.SetCollide(False)
sys.AddBody(ground)

# Visual spheres that mark the spring anchor points on the ground
marker_rad = 0.10

sph_1 = chrono.ChVisualShapeSphere(marker_rad)
ground.AddVisualShape(sph_1,
                      chrono.ChFrameD(chrono.ChVectorD(-1, 0, 0)))   # left anchor

sph_2 = chrono.ChVisualShapeSphere(marker_rad)
ground.AddVisualShape(sph_2,
                      chrono.ChFrameD(chrono.ChVectorD( 1, 0, 0)))   # right anchor

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper function: create a suspended cubical body
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def make_body(pos, color):
    body = chrono.ChBody()
    body.SetPos(chrono.ChVectorD(*pos))
    body.SetMass(1.0)
    body.SetInertiaXX(chrono.ChVectorD(1, 1, 1))
    body.SetCollide(False)

    box = chrono.ChVisualShapeBox(1, 1, 1)        # cube of edge length 2
    box.SetColor(color)
    body.AddVisualShape(box)

    sys.AddBody(body)
    return body

# Two identical bodies hanging under the ground
body_1 = make_body(pos = (-1, -3, 0), color = chrono.ChColor(0.6, 0.0, 0.0))
body_2 = make_body(pos = ( 1, -3, 0), color = chrono.ChColor(0.0, 0.0, 0.6))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Standard linear spring–damper (body_1  ↔  ground)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
spring_1 = chrono.ChLinkTSDA()
spring_1.Initialize(body_1, ground, True,
                    chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0),     # attachment in body_1 frame
                    chrono.ChVectorD(-1, 0, 0))    # attachment in ground frame
spring_1.SetRestLength(rest_length)
spring_1.SetSpringCoefficient(spring_coef)
spring_1.SetDampingCoefficient(damping_coef)
spring_1.AddVisualShape(chrono.ChVisualShapeSpring(0.05, 80, rest_length))
sys.AddLink(spring_1)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Custom force functor ------------------------------------------------------
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
class MySpringForce(chrono.ForceFunctor):
    """
    User-defined spring–damper force:
        F = −k (x − x0) − c * v
    """
    def __init__(self, k, c):
        chrono.ForceFunctor.__init__(self)
        self.k = k
        self.c = c

    def __call__(self, time, rest_length, length, vel, link):
        return -self.k * (length - rest_length) - self.c * vel

user_force = MySpringForce(spring_coef, damping_coef)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
#    Spring with custom force (body_2 ↔ ground)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
spring_2 = chrono.ChLinkTSDA()
spring_2.Initialize(body_2, ground, True,
                    chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0),     # attachment in body_2 frame
                    chrono.ChVectorD( 1, 0, 0))    # attachment in ground frame
spring_2.SetRestLength(rest_length)
spring_2.RegisterForceFunctor(user_force)
spring_2.AddVisualShape(chrono.ChVisualShapeSpring(0.05, 80, rest_length))
sys.AddLink(spring_2)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Irrlicht visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(sys)
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)
vis.SetWindowTitle("ChLinkTSDA demo with custom force functor")
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile("logo_pychrono_alpha.png"))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 10))
vis.AddTypicalLights()

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simulation loop
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()
    sys.DoStepDynamics(time_step)
```

Explanation of major fixes / additions
• Replaced obsolete calls (`SetFixed`, `EnableCollision`, `ChFramed`, etc.) with the current API equivalents.  
• All vectors are created with `chrono.ChVectorD`, the class used by the latest PyChrono builds.  
• Added class `MySpringForce` that inherits from `chrono.ForceFunctor` and returns a linear spring-damper force.  
• Added a second dynamic body (`body_2`) and its spring (`spring_2`) that relies on the custom force functor.  
• Mirrored ground-mounted visual spheres (`sph_1` and `sph_2`) to mark both attachment locations.
